WebUI

SoulX-Singer ships with two interactive browser-based interfaces built with Gradio. These are the easiest way to experiment with the model without writing code.

SVS WebUI

The SVS interface accepts lyrics, a timbre prompt, and MIDI/F0 control inputs, and returns synthesized audio.

Open your browser at http://localhost:7860 once the server is running.

Interface Panels

PanelDescription
Prompt AudioUpload a reference vocal for timbre cloning (5–15 sec)
LyricsEnter text in Mandarin, English, or Cantonese
MIDI UploadUpload a .mid file for score-mode control
F0 ContourAlternatively, upload an extracted F0 CSV/npy for melody-mode control
LanguageSelect zh, en, or yue
OutputPlays synthesized audio; download button provided

SVC WebUI

The SVC interface accepts a source singing audio and a target timbre prompt, and returns the converted audio.

Open your browser at http://localhost:7860.

Interface Panels

PanelDescription
Source AudioUpload the singing you want to convert
Prompt AudioUpload a reference vocal for the target timbre
OutputPlays converted audio; download button provided

Online Demo

You can try both modes without any local setup at the official Hugging Face Space:

https://huggingface.co/spaces/Soul-AILab/SoulX-Singer

The online demo supports both SVS and SVC modes as of March 2026.

MIDI Editor

A standalone MIDI Editor is available for correcting note alignments before inference:

https://huggingface.co/spaces/Soul-AILab/SoulX-Singer-Midi-Editor

How to use:

  1. Run the preprocessing pipeline to generate initial metadata JSON.
  2. Upload the JSON to the MIDI Editor.
  3. Use the piano-roll view to adjust note boundaries and pitches.
  4. Download the corrected metadata.
  5. Upload to the SVS WebUI or pass to infer.sh.

Running on a Remote Server

If running the WebUI on a headless server, expose it with Gradio's built-in share feature:

Performance Notes

HardwareSVS InferenceSVC Inference
NVIDIA A100~3s per segment~2s per segment
NVIDIA RTX 4090~5s per segment~3s per segment
CPU (no GPU)Very slow, not recommendedVery slow, not recommended

GPU acceleration is strongly recommended. The model requires at least 16 GB VRAM for comfortable inference; 24 GB for large batches.
